title: The Bear House — Cotton-Linen vs Pure Linen, Chinos & the ₹2,999 Cart (2026)
description: What the live catalogue actually labels: cotton-linen shirts, pure-linen elevated shirts, Oxford categories and ₹1,299 trousers — plus an honest ₹2,999 cart builder.

forWho: Indian men building a smart-casual wardrobe who want to know whether a 'linen shirt' is pure linen or a cotton-linen blend before paying.
Shoppers trying to assemble a three-piece cart near ₹2,999 without assuming an old coupon still applies.
skipIf: Anyone who needs a certified fibre percentage or mill origin — the product cards we checked gave names and categories, not lab certificates.
Buyers looking for winter-weight formal suiting; the current edit is summer-weight shirts and trousers.

content_blocks.heading: Are The Bear House linen shirts pure linen, and does the ₹2,999 coupon still work?
content_blocks.body: The live 'Linen Shirts for Men' collection mixes labels: most cards say 'Cotton Linen' and were listed at ₹999 against ₹2,495–₹2,599 MRP, while four 'Pure Linen Elevated Slim Fit Casual Shirt' cards were listed at ₹3,499. Trousers were listed from ₹1,299. The old BEAR10, BUNDLE500 (₹2,999) and EXTRA5 claims were NOT verified — the site's Black Friday banner said 'No code needed'. Build the cart from live prices, not from the old coupon.

items.title: Cotton-linen shirts — most of the 'linen' collection
items.body: The collection showed 29 products, and the majority of cards we read were explicitly labelled 'Cotton Linen' or 'Cotton-Linen' — for example a cream striped cotton-linen shirt and slim-fit cotton-linen casual shirts listed at ₹999 against ₹2,495 or ₹2,599 MRP. That is a blend label, not a pure-linen claim. If you want the feel of linen without the creasing, that is often the more practical buy; just do not pay a pure-linen premium for it.

items.title: Pure linen — the elevated tier
items.body: Four cards were labelled 'Pure Linen Elevated Slim Fit Casual Shirt' in blue, pink, navy and brown, listed at ₹3,499. These are the pieces that actually carry the pure-linen label on the pages we checked. We did not find a fibre certificate, and the site card does not state a percentage, so treat 'Pure Linen' as the brand's product label rather than an independently verified composition.

items.title: Oxford and office-wear categories
items.body: The site's shirt filter includes Oxford, Plain, Checks, Office Wear, Striped, Printed, Flannel and Half Sleeves, and the homepage popular searches include 'Oxford Shirts for Men'. We verified that these categories exist; we did not verify any fabric composition, weight or 'four-way stretch' claim from the older guide. Read the exact product page before assuming a shirt is heavier or more durable than the linen line.

items.title: Trousers and chinos — what was actually priced
items.body: The Trousers collection showed 190 products. Cards included 'TALON-BL Blue Solid Elevated Regular Fit Casual Trousers' at ₹1,299 against ₹2,299 MRP, and 'LOOPER' loose-fit casual trousers at ₹1,299 against ₹2,599. The old guide's '75/25 linen-cotton chinos' composition claim was not visible on these cards, so it is not repeated as fact. Sizes shown on the homepage ranged S to 3XL on sale shirts.

items.title: ₹2,999 cart builder — the one-rupee trap
items.body: Here is a useful original calculation from the observed prices. Three cotton-linen shirts at ₹999 each total ₹2,997 — two rupees short of the old ₹2,999 BUNDLE500 threshold. Adding one ₹1,299 trouser takes the cart to ₹3,297, which clears that old threshold on paper. But BUNDLE500 was NOT verified on 26 Nov 2026 and the live banner said 'No code needed', so build the cart on real sale prices and only count a coupon if the checkout accepts it.

items.body: Start with the label: cotton-linen shirts and pure-linen shirts sit in the same collection but at very different listed prices (₹999 versus ₹3,499 on 26 Nov 2026).
If you are near a cart threshold, remember the one-rupee trap: three ₹999 shirts are ₹2,997, not ₹2,999. Add a ₹1,299 trouser if you want a three-piece outfit rather than chasing a coupon.
Do not rely on BEAR10, BUNDLE500 or EXTRA5. We could not verify any of them; the live Black Friday banner said 'No code needed, COD available'.
Check the size chart before ordering — the site shows S to 3XL on sale shirts, and 'slim fit' is used across multiple categories.
Compare the final payable amount and the return/exchange terms with the tracked link; a lower badge price is not the whole cost.
For pure linen, expect creasing. Cotton-linen blends are usually the easier daily-wear choice in Indian humidity, but we did not handle either fabric.

content_blocks.text: We checked The Bear House homepage and its Linen Shirts and Trousers collections on 26 Nov 2026, recording displayed product labels and prices. The older guide's '100% Pure Linen', '75/25 linen-cotton chinos', Gujarat mill and stretch claims, and its BEAR10/BUNDLE500/EXTRA5 codes, were not verified and are not asserted here. We make no durability or fabric-performance claim. Durza earns a commission on qualifying purchases through tracked links at no extra cost to you.

items: 'Cotton Linen' and 'Pure Linen' are different labels on the same collection — read the card before comparing prices.
A ₹999 sale price against a ₹2,495 MRP is a displayed discount, not a verified value-for-money judgement.
Three ₹999 items total ₹2,997; one extra rupee changes whether an old ₹2,999 threshold is met, so use actual cart totals.
Slim fit appears across multiple categories; check the specific size chart rather than relying on a letter size from another brand.
Codes can expire or be replaced by automatic sale pricing. The checkout panel is the only reliable evidence.

items.q: Are The Bear House linen shirts 100% pure linen?
items.a: Not as a blanket claim. On 26 Nov 2026 the Linen Shirts collection showed mostly 'Cotton Linen' cards at ₹999 and four 'Pure Linen Elevated Slim Fit Casual Shirt' cards at ₹3,499. Check the exact product card. We did not verify any fibre percentage or certificate.

items.q: Does BUNDLE500 (₹500 off above ₹2,999) still work?
items.a: We could not verify it. The live homepage banner said 'No code needed' during the Black Friday sale. A useful cart note: three ₹999 shirts come to ₹2,997, so even the old threshold would not have been met without adding something. Only trust a coupon the checkout actually accepts.

items.q: What is the cheapest way to build a three-piece outfit?
items.a: From observed prices, two cotton-linen shirts at ₹999 each plus a ₹1,299 trouser came to ₹3,297. Three shirts at ₹999 came to ₹2,997. These are dated snapshots — compare the final payable amount with the tracked link rather than assuming the same prices next week.

We could not verify that. The Trousers collection showed regular and loose-fit casual trousers at ₹1,299, but the cards we read did not state a 75/25 linen-cotton composition. Read the exact product page before buying on that assumption.

items.q: Did Durza handle or test these fabrics?
items.a: No. We read official collection pages on 26 Nov 2026, bought nothing and make no claims about fabric weight, stretch, shrink or durability.
